Based on the verified Quranic data, here is how you can explain Tawhid to a non-Muslim, using the direct guidance from the Quran:

### 1. Start with a Common Foundation
The Quran instructs us to begin with a unifying statement when speaking to People of the Book, which can be extended as a principle for all:
> **"Say, ‘People of the Book, let us arrive at a statement that is common to us all: we worship God alone, we ascribe no partner to Him, and none of us takes others beside God as lords.’"** (Quran 3:64)

This verse provides a perfect starting point. You can say: "Let's agree on one basic principle: that there is only one Supreme God worthy of all worship, and we should not treat anything else—whether idols, desires, or people—as divine alongside Him."

### 2. Explain the Core Message
The essence of Tawhid is the absolute oneness and uniqueness of God. The Quran is clear:
> **"He is the Living One and there is no god but Him, so call on Him, and dedicate your religion entirely to Him."** (Quran 40:65)
> **"Do not call out to any other god beside God, for there is no god but Him."** (Quran 28:88)

You can explain: "Tawhid means recognizing that God is the only eternal, self-sufficient Creator. He has no partners, no children, no equals. All worship, prayer, and ultimate reliance must be directed to Him alone."

### 3. Clarify What Tawhid Rejects
Tawhid explicitly rejects associating partners with God (shirk). This includes worshiping idols, saints, or attributing divine powers to created beings:
> **"God said, ‘Do not take two gods’- for He is the One God––‘I alone am the One that you should hold in awe.’"** (Quran 16:51)
> **"Devote yourselves to God and assign Him no partners..."** (Quran 22:31)

You can say: "Islam teaches that worshiping anything besides God—whether statues, stars, or even one's own ego—distorts our innate connection to the Creator and leads us astray."

### 4. Present It as a Universal Call
Explain that this message is not new but the core of all true revelation:
> **"We sent a messenger to every community, saying, ‘Worship God and shun false gods.’"** (Quran 16:36)
> **"This is a message to all people, so that they may be warned by it, and know that He is the only God..."** (Quran 14:52)

You can add: "From Adam to Muhammad, all prophets brought the same essential message: surrender to the one true God. Tawhid is the natural faith (fitrah) ingrained in every human heart."

### 5. Invite with Clarity and Kindness
The Quran models how to present this message:
> **"Say, ‘This is my way: based on clear evidence, I, and all who follow me, call [people] to God- glory be to God!- I do not join others with Him.’"** (Quran 12:108)
> **"Say, ‘What is revealed to me is that your God is one God- will you submit to Him?’"** (Quran 21:108)

Conclude by saying: "I invite you to consider this simple, logical truth: there is only one God, and true peace comes by recognizing His oneness and living accordingly. This is the straight path."

### Key Points for Your Explanation:
- **Simplicity:** God is One, without partner, equal, or offspring.
- **Exclusivity:** All worship is for Him alone.
- **Universality:** This is humanity's innate belief and the message of all prophets.
- **Logical:** It aligns with reason—the universe points to a single, supreme Creator.
- **Practical:** It liberates from worshiping created things and directs devotion to the Creator.

Always convey this with wisdom, good manners, and patience, as the Quran instructs: **"argue only in the best way"** (Quran 29:46).
